legal_tick_units: USDC per share of a binary outcome token
legal_tick_consumer: de_fair_value_policy_seam.legal_tick() reads this key as a number; the evidence is under `legal_tick_evidence`

THE_SUB_TICK_PRICES_ARE_EXPLAINED.cause: the VENUE NARROWS THE GRID IN-WINDOW, and the tape says so
THE_SUB_TICK_PRICES_ARE_EXPLAINED.reading: every observed change is 0.01 -> 0.001. So the 0.001 levels are not a violation of the declared tick: they are the tick AFTER a `tick_size_change` event the market published. `orderPriceMinTickSize` is the tick at market creation, not for the window's life -- which is exactly the question DA 283 asked and answered too narrowly from the market record alone.
THE_SUB_TICK_PRICES_ARE_EXPLAINED.consequence_for_the_freeze: rounding to 0.01 stays LEGAL at all times, because 0.01 is a multiple of 0.001. It is not always the FINEST legal grid, so a quote on it can be improvable after a narrowing event.

legal_tick_evidence.THE_CAVEAT_IS_MEASURED: every market record declares 0.01, uniformly across all coins and both months. The BOOK does not match it exactly: 342 of 4171076 resting levels (0.0082%) sit at 0.001 granularity, in 8 of 24 sampled windows -- and those windows declare 0.01 too. So the tick is the right ROUNDING grid and is NOT a guarantee that no finer price rests on the book.
legal_tick_evidence.what_may_be_frozen_on_this: bid rounds DOWN and ask rounds UP to 0.01. A quote on that grid is legal; it is not necessarily the best price available.

maker_fee_rule.THE_SUPPORTING_RULE_SECTION_9_ASKS_FOR: the venue's own `fee_rate_bps` field, carried on every trade event in the CLOB tape and equal to 0 on all 76617 observed trades across 8 days, BTC and ETH. That is a market rule stated by the market, not an assumption.
maker_fee_rule.THE_RESIDUAL_THAT_STOPS_IT_BEING_FINAL: 10 of 1056 maker legs in the SAME markets carry a non-zero on-chain fee, all at price 0.99, in 5 transactions. 0 bps on the tape and a charge on chain cannot both be the whole story, and no collected source explains the difference. Until it is reconciled a zero fee is SUPPORTED but not SETTLED, so this module still supplies no number for §9.

per_source.searched: all top-level keys, the `clob` subobject, and the rules text (description/question/outcomes)
per_source.establishes: a per-market fee SCHEDULE field: maker_base_fee and taker_base_fee, uniform across every record
per_source.does_not_establish: the UNITS of that field, nor the rate actually applied to a fill
it is collected as a COUNT -- recv_ns and n -- so the registry's contents were never captured

per_source.searched: every payload field on every message in the sample
per_source.establishes: the VENUE's own per-trade fee rate: `fee_rate_bps`, uniformly 0 on every observed trade in these markets
per_source.does_not_establish: what would happen at a different rate; it is a record of what WAS charged, not a published schedule with an effective date

per_source.establishes: that maker fills are overwhelmingly zero-fee on chain: 1046 of 1056
per_source.does_not_establish: why the remaining 10 legs WERE charged; the audit's own role is REPORTED, NOT ENFORCED

per_source.establishes: NOTHING -- no collector names a fee schedule

WHAT_WOULD_SETTLE_IT: a reconciliation of the 10 charged legs: whether they are taker-side fees attributed to a maker address, a different fee path, or a parsing edge in the audit
or the published CLOB fee schedule for these condition ids with an effective date, which no collector currently captures
maker_fee_rule.CORRECTION_TO_DA_283: DA 283 reported this input NOT ESTABLISHABLE. That was wrong, and wrong in a way worth naming: I searched the TOP-LEVEL keys of markets.jsonl and the rewards registry and stopped. The fee was in the `clob` SUBOBJECT of every market record and in the tape's own `fee_rate_bps` on every trade. An unobtainable verdict reached by an unfinished search is a finding about the search.

initial_inventory.units: signed shares of the UP token, per market
initial_inventory.why_zero: both arms must start from the SAME state (§5 gate 6, §9's 'identical external snapshot and starting state'), and any non-zero start is a position neither arm chose. It would be carried into P&L as settlement value under §9's 'remaining inventory valued at the official settlement outcome', crediting or debiting both arms for a trade neither made.
initial_inventory.where_it_currently_lives: de_fair_value_replay_seam.replay() reads `initial_state.get('inventory', 0.0)` -- a caller-supplied value with a permissive default. Freezing it here makes the default unnecessary rather than merely convenient.
initial_inventory.the_seam_already_enforces_sharing: initial_state is a field of ReplayInputs, so two arms starting from different inventories REFUSE REPLAY_ARMS_DO_NOT_SHARE_THEIR_INPUTS -- driven in gate 6's property cells

AN_UNESTABLISHABLE_INPUT_IS_A_FINDING: two of three are established from artifacts and one is not. The one that is not is reported as a finding with the evidence that proves it unestablishable, never filled in with a plausible default.
rule_10: every number here is computed from an artifact at run time
